reason: The cited evidence (E2, E3, E5) directly supports the premise that high-strain compression induces a clustering-to-ordering transition in Al0.1CrCoFeNi, but provides no direct evidence that this SRO generates local stress fields that pin dislocations or that such pinning increases hardness/strength. The link between SRO and mechanical properties is assumed, not demonstrated, and the cited HPT study (E1) attributes hardening to second-phase refinement, not SRO.
premises: High-strain compression induces a clustering-to-ordering transition in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
Enhanced SRO/clustering generates local stress fields that pin dislocations.
SRO-induced strengthening is most effective at low to moderate Al content (x < ~0.5).
SRO can be induced by thermo-mechanical processing and quantified by APT, TEM, neutron diffraction.
SRO-induced hardening can be isolated from grain refinement and phase changes via controlled experiments.
